cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt, friends. The LORD says, "When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son." (Hosea 11:1) Notice that the love and the calling sit side by side in this one verse. That's a good thing to hold onto before the rest of this chapter gets rough.

The answer is False, and the text is blunt about it. "But the more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me." (Hosea 11:2) The more He called, the farther they went. I think that must have been a hard thing for a loving Father to watch.

The answer is the Baals, friends. Hosea 11:2 says, "They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images." Baals were false gods, and the text puts them right next to carved images. Israel was walking away from the LORD while sacrificing to the Baals.

The answer is False, and that stings a little. "…they never realized that it was I who healed them." (Hosea 11:3) The LORD took Ephraim by the arms and taught them to walk, and they never realized it was He who healed them. I think that's the kind of thing a dad remembers.

The answer is cords of kindness, friends. The LORD says, "I led them with cords of kindness, with ropes of love…" (Hosea 11:4) Ropes, and every one of them made of love. That's about as gentle as leading gets.

The answer is feed, friends. The LORD says, "I lifted the yoke from their necks and bent down to feed them." (Hosea 11:4) Think about that picture. He didn't just take the weight off, He bent down to meet them where they were.

The answer is that they refused to repent, friends. "Will they not return to the land of Egypt and be ruled by Assyria because they refused to repent?" (Hosea 11:5) Assyria is the one named to rule them. The reason is the refusing, nothing else.

The answer is True, and it's a sober one. "Though they call to the Most High, He will by no means exalt them." (Hosea 11:7) The Most High is another name for God. I think this is a heavy verse, so let's just let it be heavy for a second. And remember, friends, the story isn't over.

The answer is "How could I give you up," friends! After all of that, the LORD asks, "How could I give you up, O Ephraim?" (Hosea 11:8) Then the next line asks, "How could I surrender you, O Israel?" Right after the hard warnings comes a question full of love.

The answer is compassion, friends. The LORD says, "My heart is turned within Me; My compassion is stirred!" (Hosea 11:8) That's God speaking about His own heart. The warnings were real, and so is this.

The answer is False, and I'm glad it is. The LORD says, "I will not execute the full fury of My anger; I will not destroy Ephraim again." (Hosea 11:9) The text says it plainly, and it comes right after the warnings.

The answer is that He is God and not man, friends. "For I am God and not man—the Holy One among you—and I will not come in wrath." (Hosea 11:9) The reason is who He is. Nothing Ephraim did gets listed as the cause.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, "…I am God and not man—the Holy One among you—and I will not come in wrath." (Hosea 11:9) He calls Himself the Holy One among them. And the words right after are "I will not…"
The answer is a lion, friends! "They will walk after the LORD; He will roar like a lion." (Hosea 11:10) The text puts the roar and the walking together. And the whole thing is about what comes next.

The answer is False, friends. "When He roars, His children will come trembling from the west." (Hosea 11:10) They come trembling, and the text never says they run away. I think those must be some shaky steps. But they are steps in the right direction.

The answer is in their homes, friends. The LORD says, "Then I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD." (Hosea 11:11) Settled, and in their own homes. The one who calls them is the one who puts them there.
